text:
Let me work through this.

**Starting material:** trans-cinnamaldehyde = C6H5-CH=CH-CHO (9 carbons)

**Step 1:** MeMgBr adds to the aldehyde → secondary alcohol
C6H5-CH=CH-CH(OH)-CH3 (product 1)
Carbons: 9 + 1 = 10 carbons

**Step 2:** PCC oxidizes the secondary alcohol to a ketone
C6H5-CH=CH-CO-CH3 (product 2)
This is an α,β-unsaturated ketone (benzylideneacetone), 10 carbons

**Step 3:** (Dimethyl(oxo)-λ6-sulfaneylidene)methane = dimethylsulfoxonium methylide (Corey-Chaykovsky reagent), the sulfur ylide (CH3)2S(O)=CH2.

This reagent with an α,β-unsaturated ketone (enone) does conjugate addition to form a **cyclopropane ring** (unlike the sulfonium ylide which gives epoxide). The methylide adds a CH2 across the C=C double bond forming a cyclopropane.

Product 3: cyclopropyl ketone — C6H5-cyclopropane ring-CO-CH3
Adding one CH2 to the 10-carbon enone → 11 carbons.

**Answer:** 10 + 1 = 11 carbons

Answer: A
